note: 'Tarixdə bu gün' events used, by MM-DD. Next year pick a DIFFERENT event for the same date.

10-17.event: Bobby Fischer's 'Game of the Century' vs Donald Byrne (age 13, queen sacrifice, mate in 41)

10-18.event: Tennis for Two shown at Brookhaven visitors' day (early entertainment video game)

10-19.event: Santos-Dumont wins the Deutsch Prize: airship No. 6 round the Eiffel Tower in 29 min 30 s

10-20.event: Sydney Opera House opened by Queen Elizabeth II (budget A$7m -> A$102m, Utzon never saw it finished)

10-21.event: Guggenheim Museum (Frank Lloyd Wright) opens in New York; 16 years of work, Wright died 6 months before opening

10-22.event: André-Jacques Garnerin: first parachute descent from a balloon, Parc Monceau, Paris (~900 m, basket under canopy)

10-23.event: Apple iPod unveiled by Steve Jobs (25th anniversary): 5 GB, 1,000 songs, $399

10-24.event: Annie Edson Taylor, 63-year-old teacher, first to survive Niagara Falls in a barrel (on her birthday; test cat survived)

10-25.event: Windows XP launched in New York by Bill Gates (25th anniversary); Bliss wallpaper story (O'Rear 1996, flew the film himself)

10-26.event: The Football Association founded in London (26 Oct 1863), Morley's laws, rugby split, first game Barnes-Richmond 0-0

10-27.event: New York City Subway opened (27 Oct 1904, 2:35 pm), 28 stations, 9.1 mi, nickel fare, >100,000 riders, Mayor McClellan drove; City Hall station closed 1945

10-28.event: Statue of Liberty dedicated (28 Oct 1886, Cleveland); 350 pieces in 214 crates (Isère, 1885), 2.4 mm copper skin, Eiffel frame, Pulitzer >100,000 donors ~$1, brown -> green

10-29.event: First ARPANET message: 'login' -> only 'LO' arrived before crash (UCLA -> SRI, ~22:30, Charley Kline, ~500 km)

10-30.event: Orson Welles 'War of the Worlds' radio play (CBS, 30 Oct 1938); 'mass panic' largely a newspaper myth (Hooper survey: 2% of 5,000 households listening)

10-31.event: Mount Rushmore carving officially completed (4 Oct 1927 – 31 Oct 1941; 60 ft faces, ~400 workers, no deaths)

11-01.event: John Adams first president to live in the White House (1 Nov 1800); unfinished house, Abigail dried laundry in the East Room; 'White House' official name 1901

11-02.event: Hughes H-4 Hercules ('Spruce Goose') only flight, Long Beach Harbor: ~21 m high, ~1.6 km; 97.5 m wingspan, mostly birch, $23m, never flew again

11-03.event: Chevrolet Motor Car Company founded 3 Nov 1911 by Louis Chevrolet + William Durant; Louis sold his share 1915, returned to GM's Chevrolet division as an employee 1936

11-04.event: 4 Nov 1922: first step of the stairway to Tutankhamun's tomb KV62 uncovered (Carter, funded by Carnarvon's last season); water boy story told as 'deyilənə görə'; 26 Nov 'wonderful things'; 5 000+ items, ~10 years to clear

11-05.event: 5 Nov 1895: George Selden granted US patent 549,160 for a gasoline road engine he never built (filed 1879, ~16 years); Ford fought it 8 years, restricted 1911

11-06.event: 6 Nov 1869: first intercollegiate football game, Rutgers 6-4 Princeton at New Brunswick NJ; 25 a side, round ball, no running with the ball, ~100 spectators; Princeton won the 13 Nov rematch 8-0

11-07.event: 7 Nov 1885: Donald Smith drove the CPR last spike at Craigellachie BC, 9:22 a.m.; first spike bent and was replaced; ordinary iron spike; ~4 800 km line finished in ~5 of the 10 years allowed
